CRITICAL (1)
  * aws_s3_bucket.exports will be destroyed, losing every object and object version in the bucket [PLAN-DATA-001]
    The S3 bucket is destroyed because it is no longer in the configuration. force_destroy = true, so all objects and versions are deleted first without asking.
    -> If removing it is intended, take a backup or snapshot first and keep it until the change has settled. If it was renamed or moved in code, add a moved block instead of recreating it.

HIGH (2)
  * aws_db_instance.app will be destroyed, losing the database and everything stored in it [PLAN-DATA-001]
    The RDS database instance is destroyed because it is no longer in the configuration. Automated backups are disabled (backup_retention_period = 0). Deletion protection is on, so AWS will refuse the delete and the apply will fail before anything is lost; a final snapshot will be taken first, so the data can be restored.
    -> If removing it is intended, take a backup or snapshot first and keep it until the change has settled. If it was renamed or moved in code, add a moved block instead of recreating it.
  * aws_dynamodb_table.orders will be destroyed, losing every item in the table [PLAN-DATA-001]
    The DynamoDB table is destroyed because it is no longer in the configuration. Deletion protection is off. Point-in-time recovery is on, so AWS keeps a system backup for 35 days after deletion that can be restored to a new table.
    -> If removing it is intended, take a backup or snapshot first and keep it until the change has settled. If it was renamed or moved in code, add a moved block instead of recreating it.
